title: Habit-Driven Impact Log — Amina Hassan
content:
Purpose: lightweight, habit-focused tracker that ties daily rituals to measurable contribution metrics. Not a formal OKR doc — more of an experimental bridge between habits and visible outputs (PRs merged, docs updated, async reviews done).

Timeframe: Feb 2026 (rolling monthly view)

Why this exists:
- I get stuck optimizing for vague outcomes. Small repetitive habits should nudge larger KPIs (latency toy projects, doc churn reductions, oncall calm).
- Want a simple hypothesis test: if I do X habit 5x/week, then I should see Y output after 3 weeks.

Hypotheses / Mini-goals (measurable):
1) Daily 45-minute deep block focused on codebase or experiments -> +1 PR merged per week on average (target 4 PRs in Feb).
2) 15-minute doc sprint every morning -> reduce stale doc list by 25% (target: 6 doc edits/productions).
3) 10-minute async review window after lunch -> raise review throughput by 30% (target: 12 reviews accepted).

Baseline (Jan observations):
- PRs merged per week (personal): 0.8
- Docs edited/created: 2 total
- Reviews completed: 5

Weekly log (habit ticks and outputs)
Week 1 (Feb 1–7):
- Habit adherence: deep blocks 4/5 days, doc sprints 6/7, review windows 3/5.
- Outputs: 1 small bugfix PR merged (PR#493), updated runtime doc draft, 2 reviews.
- Quick note: deep blocks felt fragmented first two days due to meetings — moved meetings out of morning.

Week 2 (Feb 8–14):
- Habit adherence: deep blocks 5/5, doc sprints 5/5, review windows 4/5.
- Outputs: 2 PRs merged (opt/kv-cache cleanup PR#502, perf test harness PR#504), 3 docs updated, 4 reviews.
- Signal: maintaining morning cadence increases contiguous work time; small wins compound.

Week 3 (Feb 15–21):
- Habit adherence: deep blocks 5/5, doc sprints 3/5 (travel), review windows 5/5.
- Outputs: 1 experimental PR (bench experiment, WIP), 1 PR merged, 5 reviews completed.
- Signal: travel kills doc sprint but review window preserved.

Week 4 (Feb 22–28):
- Habit adherence: deep blocks 4/5, doc sprints 4/5, review windows 5/5.
- Outputs: 1 PR merged, updated RFC for a small telemetry tweak, 3 reviews.

Aggregate month outcome (Feb):
- PRs merged: 5 (target 4) -> win
- Docs edited/created: 7 (target 6) -> win
- Reviews completed: 14 (target 12) -> win

Interpretation:
- Hypotheses held up for Feb: consistent deep blocks correlate with more merges.
- Doc sprints: noisy but still net positive; batching fewer sessions when traveling still worked when paired with evening micro-sprints.
- Reviews: explicit post-lunch window drove throughput.

What went well:
- Blocking mornings and protecting them from recurring syncs helped.
- Keeping a lightweight checklist (start, stop, focus) lowered friction to begin a block.

What to change / experiments for Mar:
- Make one 2-hour weekly "zero inbox + doc tidy" session to avoid travel-induced doc drops.
- Replace one daily 45m deep block with a 90m block twice a week to push through bigger refactors.
- Track context switches per day (quick manual tally) to quantify interruptions vs outputs.

Open questions / risks:
- Is PR count the right leading indicator for broader impact (docs, mentoring, architecture)? Might overvalue small merges.
- Team bandwidth changes (oncall rotations) in March could confound habit->output mapping.

Action items (short):
- Create weekly template in Notion for rapid end-of-week log (TODO: link to template) — due 2026-03-05.
- Schedule weekly 2-hour doc tidy in calendar: recur Fridays 10–12 starting 2026-03-06.
- Trial 90m deep-blocks on Tue/Thu mornings for two weeks, log perceived progress.

Quick heuristics I used (so I can reuse):
- If habit adherence >= 80% for two consecutive weeks, assume signal; else treat as noisy.
- Convert qualitative wins into a single numeric: "visible outputs" = merges + docs + (reviews / 3). Use this for month-to-month trending.

Month-to-month snapshot (quick):
- Jan visible-outputs score = 0.8*4? (calc messy) — ledger kept locally.
- Feb visible-outputs score = merges(5) + docs(7) + reviews(14)/3 => 5 + 7 + 4.6 = 16.6 -> clear improvement from Jan.

Random notes / friction points:
- Meetings creeping back into blocked time when people ping for async comments. Need better meeting-free marker in calendar and a tiny auto-reply.
- Sometimes deep blocks became too focused on small refactors; balance with incremental shipping pressure.

Short retrospective (end of Feb):
- Hypothesis-driven, light instrumentation approach worked.
- Behaviorally the simplest change (protect mornings) had the biggest impact.
- Keep the framing: habits -> leading indicators -> visible outputs.

Links and refs (work artifacts):
- PRs: PR#493, PR#502, PR#504 (refer to linked_artifacts for one example)
- Slack thread: #eng-life / TS-324 (quick context on morning protection)
- Personal notes: weekly pages in Notion (private)

If I forget this: one sentence to self -> protect morning blocks, ship small, document often.
